name: Active keyboards and input languages
plain: Lists enabled keyboards: open on Android, a Required Reason API on iOS.
meaning: Third-party keyboards and extra input languages identify bilingual or non-native users and are a strong personalization fingerprint (Kurtz et al.).

android.note: List of IME package IDs and subtypes

ios.api_surface: Reason codes 3EC4.1 (custom keyboard app), 54BD.1 (adjust UI for active keyboards); no off-device use

limits.headline: Can see which keyboards and input languages you turned on
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app checks your keyboard setup
can: List enabled keyboards and their languages on Android
Check for a custom keyboard app, with a reason, on iPhone
Show text or tips that fit the keyboard in use
cannot: See what you type on the keyboard
Use the list on iPhone without an approved reason code
limits.differs: Android lists them with no gate. iPhone requires a declared reason code (3EC4.1 or 54BD.1).

story.what_it_is: An app can see which keyboards and input languages you turned on.
story.for_you: You never see it. Apps may show the right layout for your language. But two keyboards say more about you than you might think, like a second language or a custom one.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to show the right input screen. Ad and fraud tools also treat the keyboard list as a fingerprint, since a third party keyboard or a second language makes you stand out. It also hints at origin and language skills.

use_cases.example: A chat app shows a right to left layout when you add an Arabic or Hebrew keyboard.
A language app notices you have a Japanese keyboard and offers kana practice.
A social app suggests posts in your second language.
A keyboard app checks if it is enabled so it can show a setup guide.
An ad company infers that you are bilingual or an expat from the keyboard list.
A fraud tool compares keyboards with the account's claimed country to catch fake sign ups.

story.android_note: Android apps can list enabled input methods with few limits.
story.ios_note: iPhone apps can read this only with an approved Apple reason, and the list is meant to stay on device.

technical_bounds: iOS keyboard info needs a declared reason

history.change: Active keyboards declared Required Reason API
